sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric

announcements.name: Rayfin code-first SDK and CLI
announcements.shortDescription: Provides a TypeScript SDK for defining data models, roles, and permissions in code, plus a CLI that streamlines local development and deployment to Fabric
announcements.longDescription: Rayfin [inferred] provides a code-first SDK that makes it easier to define your data models, roles, and permissions directly on the data itself. It also includes a CLI that streamlines local development and deployment to Microsoft Fabric. Because apps deploy to Fabric, they inherit Fabric's enterprise-grade security, governance, and other capabilities.

announcements.name: Template-based scaffolding via `npm create`
announcements.shortDescription: A single command picks a starter template that pre-bakes dependencies and the agent "skills" needed to work seamlessly with coding agents
announcements.longDescription: A simple application can be created by running an npm create command, which prompts you to start from a template and pick the one you want. Because you start from a template, dependencies are pre-baked, so setup takes a while but a lot of configuration is handled for you. The templates also include the skills and context needed to work seamlessly with any coding agent, so the agent can build the application the way the SDK expects.

announcements.name: One-command deploy with `rayfin up`
announcements.shortDescription: Deploying provisions a managed database, static content hosting, and a Fabric single sign-on auth service without custom configuration
announcements.longDescription: Running the deploy command (shown as "rayfin up" [inferred]) presents the available options and provisions the backend automatically. At the back end it deploys a database, static content hosting, and an auth service, where auth is Fabric single sign-on. These services are baked in without the developer having to do any custom configuration or setup.

announcements.name: Deployment as a Fabric item
announcements.shortDescription: Rayfin apps are Fabric workspace items that inherit the workspace's capacity, CU billing model, and permission/sharing model
announcements.longDescription: In response to a question about deploying to a capacity, the speaker explains that a Rayfin app is an item inside Fabric, just like other Fabric workspace items called "app." You can create the item in any workspace, and whatever capacity that workspace is attached to is the capacity the application uses, following the same CU billing model. Under-the-hood services include the Fabric SQL database and the hosting/reference service, but you are only charged for some of the child services.

announcements.name: Embedded Fabric portal view
announcements.shortDescription: Beyond the browser, apps render inside the Fabric portal for internal/line-of-business scenarios
announcements.longDescription: Beyond running in the browser, a Rayfin application also offers an embedded view that can be rendered inside the Fabric portal, which is useful for internal/line-of-business applications. The embedded view exposes the properties and controls needed to manage the application, while the local development life cycle remains in VS Code. Because it runs in Fabric, it can talk to production data and uses Fabric single sign-on without manual database or auth setup.

announcements.name: Awesome Rayfin community template repo
announcements.shortDescription: The demo's "field engineer" template is checked in and open to community contributions; any GitHub URL containing a Rayfin template (including private ones) can be passed to `npm create`
announcements.longDescription: The field engineer template used for the demo is checked into the "awesome Rayfin" [inferred] repo, which accepts community contributions for templates and other items. You can try the demo by following the instructions to install the field engineer template via a simple npm create command that passes the template you want to use. The same pattern works by passing any GitHub URL that contains a Rayfin template, including private template marketplaces inside your own company.
